title: Inexact Bregman Sparse Newton Method for Efficient Optimal Transport
claim: Our solver reaches far lower optimality gap in less wall-clock time than first- and second-order baselines across problem sizes and data types.
layout: 2x3 grid of line plots, rows by data type, columns by problem size
description: A 2-row by 3-column grid of log-scale line plots. Top row is Uniform synthetic data and bottom row is Square data. Columns show growing problem sizes (m=n=1000, 5000, 10000). Each panel plots optimality gap (y, log scale) against time in seconds (x) for six solvers: PINS, IPOT, IBSink, HOT, ExtraGrad and IBSN. Baselines are dashed lines in blue, green, purple, pink and olive. The proposed IBSN is a solid cyan line that drops fastest and ends lowest, usually well below every baseline. HOT is noisy and oscillating, and ExtraGrad stays high and flat. Each panel has its own legend in the upper right and a title above it. The eye goes first to the solid cyan curve at the bottom left of each panel.
caption: Performance of different algorithms on synthetic data. Top: Uniform. Bottom: Square.
abstract: Computing exact optimal transport (OT) distances at large scale remains computationally challenging. Entropy-regularized OT can be solved efficiently, but its solution is biased toward the regularized problem, and small regularization parameters often lead to slow convergence and numerical instability. In this paper, we propose \emph{Inexact Bregman Sparse Newton} (IBSN), an efficient method for high-accuracy computation of the original OT problem. Building on a verifiable inexact Bregman proximal framework, IBSN develops a sparse Newton inner solver tailored to the semi-dual formulation, which yields a lower-dimensional Newton system. To accelerate the inner subproblem solves, we introduce a Hessian sparsification strategy tailored to the semi-dual formulation, which reduces the cost of Newton direction computation while preserving key spectral properties. We establish convergence guarantees for the resulting algorithm, including convergence of the inner sparse Newton iterations and global convergence of the overall method to an optimal OT solution. Numerical experiments on synthetic and real datasets show that IBSN is effective in high-accuracy regimes and compares favorably with representative first-order and second-order OT solvers.
